title: Exceptionally Mundane
html:
I was training jiu-jitsu the other day with a lad in his 40s — veteran, ripped, all-around great guy. He’s one of my favorite training partners.

He told me that one of his friends struggles to train regularly because of how much he loses, and how frustrated it makes him. I snickered as if to say, “Welcome to life, pal.”

In between reps of double-leg takedowns, my training partner said that his friend thought people who “stick with jiu-jitsu” and “get good” are cut from a different cloth — that they’ve got some special sauce that he doesn’t have.

As someone who is currently “sticking with jiu-jitsu”, my eyes nearly rolled back inside my head when I heard this.

We have no special sauce. We’re just stubborn.

We get beat up and come back for more.

That’s life.

Achieving excellence in jiu-jitsu, or any domain, is simple (not easy… simple), and it requires two steps:

  1. Show up.

  2. Repeat.

“Time under tension over time,” as another friend likes to say. Excellence comes from doing unimpressive, monotonous, and mundane things for exceptional amounts of time.

What happens if you do something once?

Nothing.

What about twice?

Nothing.

What about every day for a decade?

Now you’re elite.

Recently, I’ve been inching my way through school while sneaking in weight-lifting and jiu-jitsu to keep myself sane. Most of my weeks look the same: lift, school, jiu-jitsu. And since May 2023, when people ask what I’ve been up to, my answer has been about the same, “Lift, school, jiu-jitsu.” While it may seem dull at a glance, narrowing my focus to a few things allows me to dive deeply into all of them. And, for me, deep dives bring me the deepest joy.

If I persist over time, I’ll eventually be a jacked, PhD, black belt, without ever doing anything extraordinary in a day. I’m just stacking pennies.

So, this is a reminder (to myself, mostly,) to be patient, take your time, and just keep showing up. You don’t need to cram more into each day to be great. You just need to live more days.

Oh, and don’t forget that this moment, and these breaths, are your life too. It doesn’t start when you achieve some arbitrary goal like getting a PhD or a black belt. So, if you want to enjoy your life, you’ll only ever be able to do it now.

Right now.
